Muzhou Daoming ends his exchange with the scripture lecturer by giving the household comparison after the lecturer falls silent. Occurrences.Kwic: 雄峰。僧云：恁麼則主山高，案山低也。師云：一切坐斷。乃云：佛語心為宗，一切即一；無門為法門，一即一切。是汝諸人高肩拄杖，天下橫行，還踏著此門也未？若也踏著此門，年年是好年，月月是好月，日日是好日，時時是好時，明如杲日，寬若太虗。三世諸佛以此門生凡育聖，廣利羣品；歷代祖師以此門以心契心，流通正續；天下宗祖以此門揭示人天眼目，提持向
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X84/X84n1583.xml). Orthodox Continuation of the Lamp records Huqiu Shaolong extending the good-year formula through months, days, and hours.

Senses.Explanation: Every year is a good year is a New Year formula that is also paired with good months, days, and hours. An unnamed monk offers the year-and-day pair to Chushi Fanqi, whose reply compares it to a blind old woman blowing a fire. Nouyun Zhenshi uses the expanded formula to open a New Year address, while Huqiu Shaolong places it after a question about entering a gate. These passages show a recurrent saying that can be answered and tested in an encounter; they do not make it a prediction about the calendar.

Senses.Explanation: At the year's end marks the exhaustion of the old year. Tian'an Sheng and Haiyin Zhaoru use it while describing what remains at the close of the year; Huiyue Xu and Duanqiao Miaolun open New Year's Eve addresses with it. Xutang Zhiyu also folds the phrase into a criticism of practitioners who reach year's end without knowing how to turn around. Elsewhere in the record it forms the recurring question, ‘At year's end, what then?’
